At its core, Nedryland provisions new machines and synchronizes CLI preferences across computers using
. It also bundles Git workflow improvements, like automatically attaching ticket numbers to commits, generating and zipping patches, and conditionally opening the Git editor in the foreground IDE.

Beyond the shell, Nedryland is where I maintain a library of reusable skills for Claude Code and Codex. These cover the workflows I run most: creating PRs, staging and committing changes with consistent conventions, curating branch history, and reviewing Force Refresh support requests. Rather than re-prompting from scratch each time, I keep the skills here and pull them into any project.
Themes for iTerm2 and Slack are built around a Jurassic Park color palette derived from the Nedryland interface and the breaker panel in the maintenance shed.
